segments.narration: As the legend goes, every single resident vanished from an Inuit village in 1930. Fur trapper Joe Labelle paddled to the shores of Lake Anjikuni, expecting a bustling community.
Instead, he found absolute silence. Unfinished shirts still had sewing needles in them, and food hung over unlit fire pits, left as if mid-task.
Even more unsettling, seven sled dogs were found dead from starvation, and a grave appeared to have been opened without disturbing the circling stones. How does an entire settlement simply evaporate?
For decades, newspapers spun wild yarns of lights in the winter sky and ghostly abductions. Author Frank Edwards cemented the myth in his 1959 paranormal bestseller.
Yet Mountie records from the era reveal zero official reports of a missing village. Was the whole thing just an urban legend born from a lonely trapper's campfire story?
